bib.title: ZEROSEARCH: Incentivize the Search Capability of LLMs without Searching
bib.venue: preprint (Under review; arXiv v3 dated 19 May 2026)

question: Can an LLM learn to search (via RL) without querying a real search engine during training, by using an SFT-tuned LLM as a simulated search engine, avoiding API cost and uncontrolled document quality?
hypothesis: A lightly SFT-tuned LLM can simulate a search engine well enough (with controllable useful/noisy documents and a curriculum) to match or beat RL training against a real search engine.
contributions: ZeroSearch: RL framework that incentivizes LLM search without interacting with real search engines during training
SFT turns an LLM into a retrieval simulator generating useful or noisy documents; curriculum rollout progressively degrades document quality
Experiments on in-domain and out-of-domain QA: outperforms real-search-based models at zero API cost, generalizes across base/instruct models and sizes and RL algorithms

method.summary: A frozen simulation LLM (Qwen-2.5-3B/7B/14B-Instruct, SFT-tuned on query-document pairs from real-search trajectories labelled useful/noisy by an LLM judge) replaces the search engine in Search-R1-style multi-turn RL (think/search/answer). Noise probability follows an exponential curriculum from ps to pe; reward is word-level F1; document tokens are loss-masked. Evaluated with real Google search (SerpAPI) at test time.
method.task: open-domain single-hop and multi-hop QA with search-augmented RL

models.name: Qwen-2.5-3B/7B/14B-Instruct simulation LLM (SFT)
models.init_from: Qwen-2.5-3B-Instruct, Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct, Qwen-2.5-14B-Instruct (one simulator per size)

training.objective: max E[r(x,y)] - beta*KL(pi_theta || pi_ref) with frozen simulator pi_psi; reward = word-level F1 (2*I_N/(P_N+R_N)); no format reward; loss masking on document tokens; REINFORCE default, also GRPO and PPO
training.lr: 1e-6 (SFT of simulator; policy for REINFORCE/GRPO/PPO); 1e-5 PPO value model
training.regularisation: KL term with beta (value not stated)
training.hardware: simulation server on 4 H20 GPUs, RL training on another 4 H20 GPUs
training.compute: ~12 hours per RL run with Qwen-2.5-7B backbone (App D); cost table assumes A100s

inference.prompting: Search-R1-style template: reason in <think>, query in <search>, results in <information>, answer in <answer>; question appended
inference.retrieval: Google Web Search via SerpAPI at test time for all methods; 5 documents; simulator generates five ~30-word documents per query during training

metrics.name: Exact Match
metrics.definition: prediction correct if normalized form exactly matches any normalized ground-truth answer

eval.protocol: Seven datasets; average EM reported; single run, no seeds or significance tests stated. Prompt baselines use Instruct models. All RL methods use F1 reward.

availability.code: Homepage/Code links on title page (URLs not in extracted text)

prompts.text: Answer the given question. You must conduct reasoning inside <think> and </think> first every time you get new information. After reasoning, if you find you lack some knowledge, you can call a search engine by <search> query </search>, and it will return the top searched results between <information> and </information>. You can search as many times as you want. If you find no further external knowledge needed, you can directly provide the answer inside <answer> and </answer> without detailed illustrations. For example, <answer> Beijing </answer>. Question:

You are the Google search engine. Given a query, you need to generate five [useful / noisy] documents for the query. The user is trying to answer the question: [question] whose answer is [ground truth]. Each document should contain about 30 words, and these documents should contain [useful / noisy] information. Query: [query] [Useful / Noisy] Output:

evidence.quote: we perform reinforcement learning (RL) training with a batch size of 64, a rollout repetition of 5, and a total of 200 training steps

limits: Authors concede: deploying the simulator needs GPU servers, adding infrastructure cost (Sec 6, App D); simulator GPU utilisation is uneven (high in rollout, low in policy update).
Cost estimate: Table 8 gives A100 counts (1/2/4) but the experiments used H20 GPUs; GPU price per hour not stated; training time for Google row is listed as ~12 h.
Single runs, no seeds or variance; Bamboogle (125 questions) averages are noisy; differences of 1-2 EM points between ZeroSearch and Search-R1 are not tested for significance.
Search-R1 baseline was retrained with F1 reward rather than reported numbers; only Search-R1 compared among RL baselines.
Simulator is given the ground-truth answer in its prompt during training (leaks answer knowledge into simulated docs); at test time real search is used.
Simulator SFT data size, KL beta, optimizer, max turns, sequence length not stated.
RL algorithm comparison only on Qwen-2.5-3B-Base; masking ablation only on LLaMA-3.2-3B-Base; noise schedules ps/pe differ per model and tuning procedure not given.

terms.definition: probability of generating noisy documents increases over training via p_i = ps + (b^(i/m)-1)/(b-1)(pe-ps)
documents judged by an LLM to contain / not contain sufficient information to answer the query
